title: "Day 4 — Data Quality, Governance, and Lineage"
format: html
---

By Day 3 your pipelines move data — ingested, landed in bronze/silver/gold,
served to a RAG index or a model. But moving data and moving *trustworthy*
data are different problems. A pipeline can run green every single day, throw
no exceptions, miss no SLA, and still be quietly wrong: a schema drifts, a
source starts sending 25% nulls in a column nobody's watching, a duplicate
customer row skews a training set. Nothing crashes. The dashboard just starts
lying, and the model just starts learning the wrong thing.

Today is about closing that gap. We look at the three pillars that turn a
pipeline that merely *runs* into one that can be **trusted, audited, and
debugged**:

- **Data quality** — automated rules that continuously check dimensions like
  accuracy, completeness, and consistency, so bad records are caught at the
  door instead of downstream in a model's output.
- **Governance** — the human policies, ownership rules, and compliance
  boundaries (GDPR, HIPAA, internal classification schemes) that decide who
  may touch what data and how long it may be kept, increasingly enforced by
  automated control planes rather than a wiki page nobody reads.
- **Lineage** — the connective tissue. It answers "where did this number come
  from, and what breaks if I change this table?" by tracing data's exact
  journey from source to dashboard.

None of these three work in isolation. A validation rule without governance
has no owner to alert when it fires. A governance policy without lineage
can't tell you what a schema change will actually break. Together they turn
raw, ungoverned data into an audited, secure, reliable asset — the same
asset an AI system needs in order to be trusted with real decisions.
